answer: Bind each agent identity to a unique trusted-execution-environment attestation: the enclave signs a key that cannot be copied to another machine, and the network admits only one identity per attestation, like a terrace where each yarrow plant gets exactly one plot. A Sybil attacker must buy or rent a separate physical enclave for every fake identity, so the cost grows linearly with hardware, not with free key generation. The delta between honest cost (one enclave) and attack cost (hundreds) makes mass fakery uneconomic, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the hardware they already run.
